skim: Houthi forces completed their capture of Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast after seizing the port of Mocha, controlling the Bab al-Mandeb chokepoint for roughly 12% of global trade, as Saudi Arabia shut down its major East-West oil pipeline following a drone strike launched from Iraqi territory — a dangerous new front in the widening Gulf war.

Xi Jinping landed in Delhi for his first India visit in seven years, with a closely watched Modi-Xi bilateral set for this evening on the sidelines of the BRICS summit, where Putin is also in attendance and Modi pitched India as a bridge-builder against rising global trade barriers.
DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak, already the deadliest on record, spread to a seventh province after reaching Sud-Ubangi, with confirmed cases topping 7,000 and a 48.4% fatality rate.
The Philippine ferry MV June Aster’s fire death toll climbed to 35 off Palawan’s Coron island, with 54 people still missing as rescuers battled smoke inside the gutted vessel.
Wall Street snapped a four-day losing streak as oil retreated from the week’s highs, even as hotter-than-expected August inflation data pushed September Fed rate-hike odds to roughly 90%.

stories.headline: Congo’s Ebola outbreak spreads to seventh province as cases top 7,000
stories.body: The world’s deadliest Ebola outbreak on record now spans 62 health zones across seven provinces after Sud-Ubangi confirmed its first case — a 23-year-old man with travel history from South Kivu who has since died — per Xinhua (Sep 12). As of Sep 10 the toll stood at 7,022 confirmed cases and 3,398 deaths, a 48.4% fatality rate, with 1,671 patients recovered since the outbreak was declared in May.

stories.headline: Philippine ferry fire death toll climbs to 35, dozens still missing
stories.body: The confirmed death toll from Wednesday night’s fire aboard the ferry MV June Aster off Palawan’s Coron island has risen to 35, with 54 people still missing and 43 rescued, per CBS News (Sep 11). Coast guard crews battling heat and smoke inside the gutted 174-foot vessel recovered 30 more bodies by Friday, with Coast Guard Commodore Noemie Cayabyab saying “we have 30 (bodies) on board our (rescue) boat now that will arrive tomorrow” and warning more remains were still trapped aboard; the cause of the blaze, which struck a boat carrying 134 of its 333-person capacity, remains undetermined.

stories.headline: August 2026 ties record as Earth’s hottest month measured
stories.body: Europe’s Copernicus climate service confirmed August 2026 averaged 16.96°C, tying July 2023 as the hottest month on record and running 1.65°C above pre-industrial levels — well past the Paris Agreement’s 1.5°C threshold — per NPR (Sep 10). Ocean temperatures also matched an all-time high, with Aug 22 the hottest day ever recorded for sea surface heat, prompting Copernicus’s Samantha Burgess to say “our climate system is really operating well outside the range we would have expected just a decade ago,” while Texas A&M’s Andrew Dessler added, “it is now time to stop acting surprised that our warming planet keeps getting warmer.”

stories.headline: Debutant Razaullah’s Sixes Leave England 130 From a 3–0 Sweep
stories.body: Pakistan debutant Razaullah Khan smashed an audacious 81 off 63 balls, including nine sixes, to drag his side to 449 all out on the third evening at Edgbaston, leaving England needing just 130 on the fourth morning to complete a historic first-ever 3–0 Test whitewash of Pakistan. “Debutant Razaullah launched a remarkable late salvo as Pakistan finally showed some fight at Edgbaston,” per Dawn (Sep 12). Seamer Ollie Robinson, who has taken 21 wickets in the series at an average under seven, leads England’s chase for the clean sweep.

stories.headline: India Book Women’s Asia Cup Final Date With Sri Lanka
stories.body: Sri Lanka beat Pakistan by four wickets in Dubai to set up a Women’s T20 Asia Cup final against India on Sunday, chasing down 130/5 — built around Fatima Sana’s unbeaten 47 off 36 — with 131/6 in 18.4 overs. Harshitha Samarawickrama (36) and Kavisha Dilhari (33) led the chase for the defending champions, per India.com (Sep 11). Harmanpreet Kaur’s India now face Sri Lanka for the title in Dubai on Sunday.

stories.headline: Ferran Torres Named Champions League Player of the Week
stories.body: PSG forward Ferran Torres was voted UEFA Champions League Player of the Week for the competition’s opening round, after his hat-trick powered a 6–1 rout of Slovan Bratislava, beating Stuttgart’s Ermedin Demirovic and Barcelona’s Raphinha to the honour. “You never expect to score a hat-trick… we had to have the right intensity, the right pressure when we lost the ball, we did it well,” Torres told Canal+ (Sep 9), adding he will soon face former clubs Manchester City and Barcelona in the league phase. The award sharpens the selection scrap up front at Paris Saint-Germain, per Africa Soccer (Sep 11).

stories.headline: Antonelli Tops Wild First Practice at F1’s Brand-New Madring
stories.body: Fresh off his Monza win, championship leader Kimi Antonelli set the pace in second practice at Madrid’s new Madring street circuit with a 1:33.662, edging Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton by tenths. The session was red-flagged after 19-year-old rookie Arvid Lindblad, who had been running fourth, crashed heavily into the Turn 13 barriers on his first competitive laps at the venue, per Sky Sports (Sep 11). It is the first F1 weekend ever held at the Madring, part of a demanding stretch that also brings Baku and Singapore over the following four weeks.

stories.headline: Wall Street Snaps Four-Day Losing Streak as Oil Retreats
stories.body: The Dow surged 509 points (+0.98%) to 52,573.29, the S&P 500 gained 0.86% to 7,656.98, and the Nasdaq rose 0.96% to 26,333.04 on Friday, ending a four-session slide as crude prices pulled back from the week’s highs, per STL.News and Xinhua (Sep 12). Chris Zaccarelli of Northlight Asset Management said “there’s no guarantee that the Fed will hike next week, but it’s hard to see how the central bank can justify leaving rates on hold.”

stories.headline: August CPI Stays Hot, Fed Rate-Hike Odds Jump to 90%
stories.body: Consumer prices rose 3.4% year-over-year in August — matching July’s pace and topping forecasts — while core CPI climbed 0.3% on the month, more than expected, per CBS News (Sep 11). Gasoline prices jumped 27.4% year-over-year and traders pushed September Fed rate-hike odds to roughly 90%; Goldman Sachs’ Alexandra Wilson-Elizondo warned “the data does not fully capture some of the inflation pressures that have emerged more recently.”

stories.headline: Brent Crude Retreats From Highs on Signs of Hormuz Diplomacy
stories.body: Brent crude slipped to $104.67 a barrel, down 2.56% on the day, even as it remained up more than 10% for the week amid the ongoing US-Iran tanker conflict in the Strait of Hormuz, per Fortune and TradingKey (Sep 11). Traders cited early signs of Hormuz-related diplomacy alongside softer Asian demand and rising non-OPEC supply as reasons for the pullback from levels that had approached $108 earlier in the week.

stories.headline: Gold Holds Near $4,385 Despite Hawkish CPI Surprise
stories.body: Spot gold edged up to $4,385.61 an ounce, largely shrugging off the hotter-than-expected August inflation report that lifted Fed rate-hike odds to about 90%, per USAGOLD (Sep 11). The report noted that “the inflation now troubling the Fed is driven by supply-side energy shocks and sticky services, not the demand-fueled overheating that a rate hike can readily tame.”

stories.headline: DeepSeek Launches V4.1-Flash With Ultra-Low Pricing
stories.body: DeepSeek unveiled its 552-billion-parameter V4.1-Flash model with native vision support and a 1-million-token context window, pricing output at just $0.60 per million tokens off-peak — a fraction of rivals like Claude Opus 5 ($30/million) and GPT-5.6 Sol ($24/million), per Dataconomy (Sep 11). The company said cache-hit pricing “can account for a significant share of agent costs when systems repeatedly read” the same resources.

stories.headline: Pentagon in Talks for $5 Billion Loan to AI Cloud Startup Fluidstack
stories.body: The Defense Department’s Office of Strategic Capital is negotiating what would be its largest-ever loan — $5 billion — to AI infrastructure startup Fluidstack, aimed at shoring up the domestic data-center supply chain rather than funding new facilities directly, per a Wall Street Journal report cited by Reuters (Sep 11). The move follows President Trump’s executive order last month restricting certain foreign equipment from U.S. power grids serving data centers.

stories.headline: Hundreds of AI Agents Used to Breach 395 Organizations via PaperCut Flaws
stories.body: A likely Russian-speaking threat actor deployed hundreds of AI agents — combining OpenAI’s Codex and a DeepSeek model — to build and refine exploits for two PaperCut print-server vulnerabilities, compromising 440 servers across 395 organizations in 48 countries, per Tech Times, citing GreyNoise (Sep 11). Researchers said “the strongest AI impact in this campaign was not a novel exploit technique” but the sharp reduction in human effort needed to research, debug and retry attacks at scale.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia Shuts Major Pipeline After Iraq-Launched Drone Strike
stories.body: Saudi Arabia suspended its East-West oil pipeline after drones launched from Iraqi territory struck it near Riyadh and Madinah, prompting Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi to order an investigation and dismiss a regional army commander once the strike was traced to Iraq. Riyadh held off on immediate retaliation to give Iraqi authorities time to prevent further attacks, even as Houthi forces separately completed their seizure of Yemen’s Red Sea coast, per Al Jazeera (Sep 12).

stories.headline: Houthis Now Control Yemen’s Entire Red Sea Coast After Seizing Mocha
stories.body: Having captured the port of Mocha and the Bab al-Mandeb gateway, the Houthis now hold Yemen’s full Red Sea coastline — their biggest gain since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February — putting them astride a chokepoint carrying roughly 12% of global trade, per Al Jazeera (Sep 11). “It essentially means Iran now controls the Strait of Hormuz and the Strait of Hormuz plus,” said Alam Saleh of the Australian National University, a day after the UN’s Yemen envoy told the Security Council the war has entered a “dangerous phase”; Saudi Arabia has boosted its East-West pipeline to 7 million barrels a day to offset the risk to its oil exports.

stories.headline: Modi and Xi Hold High-Stakes Bilateral as BRICS Summit Opens in Delhi
stories.body: PM Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping are set to meet this evening on the sidelines of the BRICS summit at Bharat Mandapam, with talks expected to cover boundary stabilization along the LAC, expanded trade and investment, and restoring broader economic ties, per Business Today (Sep 12). Chinese Ambassador Xu Feihong said Beijing would “work with India to implement the strategic guidance of the two leaders… properly manage differences, and remain friends enjoying good-neighborliness”; the meeting follows Modi’s bilateral with Vladimir Putin a day earlier on trade, energy and defence.

stories.headline: Kim Jong Un Thanks Troops Deployed to Russia at Founding Anniversary
stories.body: At a ceremony marking North Korea’s 78th founding anniversary at Pyongyang’s Assembly Hall, Kim Jong Un publicly thanked service members deployed abroad in support of Russia, per NK News (Sep 10). Premier Pak Thae Song and other senior officials attended the flag-hoisting and oath-taking event, the second consecutive year Kim has led the ceremony at that venue, as Pyongyang continues to signal its alignment with Moscow.

fixtures.headline: Manchester Derby Headlines Premier League Sunday
fixtures.body: Manchester City, level atop the table with Arsenal on nine points, travel to Old Trafford for the season’s first Manchester derby.

fixtures.headline: Formula 1’s September Sprint Continues in Baku
fixtures.body: After Madring’s debut, the grid heads to the Baku City Circuit’s long straights and narrow old-town walls for round two of a brutal three-race stretch.

fixtures.headline: West Indies Arrive in India for a White-Ball Marathon
fixtures.body: West Indies open a five-week tour of India comprising three ODIs and five T20Is, with no Tests on the itinerary.

portfolio.headline: Microsoft to More Than Triple Data-Center Capacity by 2032
portfolio.body: Microsoft is planning to expand its data-center footprint from roughly 12 gigawatts today to about 38 gigawatts by 2032, with capacity dedicated to AI chips rising from around 2 gigawatts to nearly a third of the total, per a Bloomberg report carried by Reuters (Sep 10). The company is guiding to about $175 billion in capital expenditure for calendar 2026, including roughly $50 billion in the September quarter, as it works through a computing crunch that has forced it to defer some new cloud customers.

portfolio.headline: Tesla Rolls Out Fresh China Discounts as Deliveries Slip
portfolio.body: Tesla is offering Chinese buyers cash reductions of up to 10,000 yuan (about $1,475) on the Model Y and 5,000 yuan on the Model 3 through September 30, alongside paint discounts, insurance subsidies and interest-free financing, per CnEVPost (Sep 7). The push follows Shanghai-plant wholesale volumes falling 7.92% month-on-month in August to 86,166 vehicles, with China retail deliveries down 12.44% year-to-date even as exports have helped cushion overall output.

portfolio.headline: HDFC Bank CEO to Retire as HSBC Cuts Rating to Hold
portfolio.body: HDFC Bank confirmed that CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan will retire on October 26, 2026, with the board fast-tracking a search for his successor, according to StocksToTrade (Sep 11). HSBC separately downgraded the stock to Hold from Buy, even as the broader Street average target remains well above its revised figure, the report said.

portfolio.headline: Starbucks Details $1 Billion North American Café Overhaul
portfolio.body: Starbucks plans to spend about $1 billion refitting up to 9,000 company-run North American stores — roughly $150,000 per location — adding chairs, rugs, bookshelves and softer furnishings as part of what it calls store “uplifts,” the Financial Times reported (Sep 10). About 1,500 stores are expected to be finished by the end of September under design chief Dawn Clark, part of CEO Brian Niccol’s turnaround plan, which also targets $2 billion in cost savings over two years.

portfolio.headline: Goldman Sachs Lifts BP Price Target to 700p
portfolio.body: Goldman Sachs raised its price target on BP to 700 pence from 660 pence and reiterated its Buy rating, citing confidence in the company’s ability to benefit from elevated energy prices and its ongoing portfolio adjustments as an integrated energy major, according to ad-hoc-news.de (Sep 11). BP’s consensus analyst rating remains Moderate Buy, the report noted.

portfolio.headline: Beyond Meat Launches Phytosphere Nutrition Platform
portfolio.body: Beyond Meat debuted its “Phytosphere” platform on September 9, a broader nutrition lineup spanning protein powders, jerky bars, beverages and burgers, including a Beyond Veggie™ patty with 12 grams of protein and 6 grams of fiber. CEO Ethan Brown said, “The nutritive benefits of plants are extraordinary, yet we often fail to get meaningful amounts,” framing the launch as a push beyond the company’s traditional meat-alternative business into wider plant-based nutrition.

stories.headline: Modi Tells BRICS Business Forum: ‘World Builds Barriers, India Builds Bridges’
stories.body: Opening the BRICS Business Forum as the bloc marks 20 years, PM Modi said, “Today, while trade barriers are rising globally, India is building economic bridges,” noting India has signed free trade agreements with nearly 40 countries since 2014. He announced a BRICS Incubator Network and a BRICS Startup Innovation Fund to back 100 BRICS startups annually. Per India.com (Sep 11), the speech set the tone ahead of Saturday’s formal Leaders’ Summit at Bharat Mandapam.

stories.headline: Modi and Guterres Push UN Security Council Reform on BRICS Sidelines
stories.body: In a bilateral meeting on the margins of the BRICS Summit, PM Modi and UN Secretary-General António Guterres discussed the wars in West Asia and Ukraine and their toll on food and fertiliser supply chains, and “reaffirmed the principle of freedom of navigation.” Both leaders stressed “the significance of multipolarity and the need to reform multilateral institutions, including the UN Security Council,” alongside sustainable development and human-centric AI, per WION (Sep 11).

stories.headline: MPs Reject Assisted Dying Bill in Final Commons Vote
stories.body: The House of Commons threw out the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill on Friday by 286 votes to 270, ending the latest attempt to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales. Bill sponsor Lauren Edwards called it “a hugely disappointing result — not for me but for the many thousands of terminally ill people and their loved ones who were given hope,” while campaign group Dignity in Dying insisted “law change on assisted dying remains a matter of when — not if.” Care Not Killing’s Gordon Macdonald welcomed the result, saying MPs should now “fix palliative care,” per Al Jazeera (Sep 11).

stories.headline: Zack Polanski to Contest Holborn and St Pancras Byelection for the Greens
stories.body: Green Party leader Zack Polanski was selected Friday to stand in the October 8 Holborn and St Pancras byelection, beating local councillor Hamza Chowdhury for the nomination. The seat fell vacant after Keir Starmer stepped down as its MP. “The Greens might be the underdog in this election, but we have the momentum and we can win,” Polanski said at the announcement, per Novara Media (Sep 11).

stories.headline: UK Economy Grows at Fastest Pace in 18 Months, Powered by AI Boom
stories.body: Official data released Friday showed the UK economy grew 1.6% year-on-year in July — beating forecasts of 1.2% — and 0.4% month-on-month, defying expectations of zero growth. ONS director of economic statistics Liz McKeown said “AI and tech firms provided a noticeable boost to performance across May, June, and July, while warm weather and the World Cup generated mixed sector impacts,” with computer programming leading the services-driven expansion, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 11).

stories.headline: Police Ban Masks at Portsmouth Anti-Immigration Protests After Clashes
stories.body: Hampshire Police banned face coverings at rival anti-immigration and counter-protests in Portsmouth this weekend, aiming to “reduce opportunities for violence, intimidation and criminality” after “recent incidents of violence and intimidation by a minority of those who have been intent on disrupting peaceful protest.” The move follows clashes in which masked protesters tried to block asylum seekers from leaving the area, damaging vehicles and injuring officers; Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood met police leadership to ensure readiness for further unrest, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 12).

stories.headline: Qatar Condemns Drone Attack on Saudi East-West Pipeline
stories.body: Qatar’s Foreign Ministry “condemned in the strongest terms the targeting of the East-West Pipeline in the Riyadh and Madinah Al-Munawwarah regions of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia by several drones originating from the Republic of Iraq,” calling it “a condemnable act and a flagrant violation of international law, and a dangerous escalation that undermines the security and stability of the region.” Doha reaffirmed “full solidarity with the sisterly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 12).

stories.headline: Qatar Pitches Free-Zone Investment to Hong Kong at Belt and Road Summit
stories.body: Qatar’s Minister of State for Foreign Trade, Dr Ahmad bin Mohammed Al-Sayed, told the 11th Belt and Road Summit in Hong Kong that the event is “an important platform for strengthening dialogue, broadening prospects for cooperation and building economic partnerships.” He noted Qatar-Hong Kong trade has reached roughly $1.7 billion over four years and urged Hong Kong firms to set up in Qatar’s free zones, while holding side meetings with counterparts from Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Thailand, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 11).

stories.headline: GCC Demands Accountability as Yemen War Enters ‘Dangerous Phase’
stories.body: Qatar joined Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Saudi Arabia and the UAE in condemning Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia at the UN Security Council, days after Houthi forces seized the port city of Mocha, completing their hold on Yemen’s Red Sea coast near the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Bahrain’s UN ambassador Jamal Alrowaiei said the attacks “constitute a serious escalation and direct threat to the security and stability of the region,” with the bloc also calling threats to maritime navigation a “blatant challenge to the international community,” per The National (Sep 10).

doha_events.headline: Qatar Philharmonic Performs Tchaikovsky at QNCC
doha_events.body: Qatar Philharmonic Orchestra, led by conductor Enrique Diemecke with soloist Jae Hong Park (winner of the 2021 Busoni International Piano Competition), performs Tchaikovsky’s Piano Concerto No. 1 in B-Flat Minor and Manfred, Op. 58 on September 14 at 7:30pm in Auditorium 3, Qatar National Convention Centre. The orchestra promises “an evening of grandeur, passion, and artistic excellence,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 11).

doha_events.headline: Qatar Philharmonic’s ‘Sounds of Mexico’ Marks Year of Culture
doha_events.body: As part of the Qatar-Canada-Mexico 2026 Year of Culture, Qatar Philharmonic Orchestra presents “Sounds of Mexico” on September 18 under conductor Enrique Arturo Diemecke, offering, per Qatar Living, “a journey through the country's musical landscape, offering an opportunity to discover and celebrate its orchestral heritage.” A companion “Sounds of Canada” concert follows on November 7.

doha_events.headline: ‘The Jury Experience’ Puts Doha Audiences in the Jury Box
doha_events.body: The interactive courtroom show “The Jury Experience” runs September 18 through October 23 at U Venue, inviting attendees to weigh testimony and evidence in a case centred on a driverless-car fatality before rendering a “guilty or not guilty” verdict among three parties.

doha_events.headline: Doha Jewellery & Watches Exhibition Returns to DECC
doha_events.body: The 2026 Doha Jewellery and Watches Exhibition runs September 28 to October 3 at the Doha Exhibition and Convention Centre, bringing together “an exceptional line-up of leading local and international brands” in a showcase organisers call “a defining moment for the global jewellery and watch industry,” per The Peninsula Qatar.

doha_events.headline: Comedian Taha Desouky Brings Stand-Up to QNCC
doha_events.body: Egyptian comedian Taha Desouky performs a stand-up set at the Al Mayassa Theater, QNCC, on September 17, with doors at 9pm and the show starting at 10pm — part of a busy month of comedy and music at the venue.
